correctness_confidence.basis: Factoring the difference of squared CARs checks both absolute-value branches. The two-factor lower bound and the explicit common allocation together establish the simultaneous threshold.

rigor.basis: The argument distinguishes a first tie from an infimum for strict reversal. State whether rounding ties are admitted and link the full branch calculations alongside the exchange proof.

novelty.basis: The primary deposit contains the stock and equal-weight portfolio summaries. The contribution evaluated here is the sharp common-weights analysis of those summaries. The total-variation extremum principle is prior work.

significance.basis: The exercise establishes when an apparent attenuation is robust to changes of issuer weighting. The welfare, dispatch and electricity-demand consequences of REDATA remain unmeasured.

reproducibility.basis: Two source fetches produced identical PDF bytes and verifier outputs. The source version is linked. The PDF itself lacks a persistent link to its own exact code and certificates.

summary: I read the three rendered pages and participated in the work. The paper identifies the exact issuer reweighting needed to erase a particular two-event ranking and exhibits a strictly positive allocation reversing it under two fitted specifications. The analysis is convincing for fixed published issuer returns. Its value is as a sensitivity analysis of one result. The broad optimization principle already has a substantial literature.
strengths: Explicit allocations witness both ties and strict reversal.
The 5 to 20 percent box and the 1/24 percent construction give contrasting, interpretable exposures.
The paper states that daily missingness can alter the portfolio functional.
weaknesses: A permanent link to the exact package should appear in the PDF.
The threshold allocations have no empirical calibration to actual holdings.
The generic total-variation principle is standard and the empirical scope is limited to one pair of events.
potential_errors: The stock-only rounding interval should not be read as sharp after adding restrictions from the separately rounded portfolio totals.
Weights on stock-level CARs need not correspond to the deposit daily renormalization if event-day residuals are missing.
The percentages of mass transferred cannot be interpreted as percentages of return or probability.
strong_novelty_candidates: The two exact simultaneous exposure thresholds and an explicit positive portfolio reversing both model comparisons for REDATA.
